skill.name: secret-scanner
skill.description: Find exposed secrets in repositories and guide safe remediation.
skill.summary: Scans code and git history for exposed credentials, tokens, private keys, and other sensitive data.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged many sensitive strings, command examples, URLs, and environment variable references, but review shows they are part of a defensive secret scanning guide. No prompt injection, covert execution, credential collection, or unauthorized exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes destructive remediation examples such as history rewrites, force pushes, and remote authorized_keys edits.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to review commands, back up repositories, and coordinate with collaborators before running destructive cleanup steps.

remediation.issue: Example secrets include realistic-looking tokens and credentials that may trigger automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Mark all example values clearly as nonfunctional placeholders and prefer reserved example domains and provider-documented sample keys.

content.value_statement: Leaked credentials can give attackers access to cloud accounts, databases, and payment systems. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code find likely secrets and produce clear remediation steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common secret patterns such as AWS keys, GitHub tokens, database URLs, and private keys.
Suggests scanner commands using tools such as git-secrets, TruffleHog, Gitleaks, and detect-secrets.
Separates likely real secrets from placeholders and documentation examples.
Produces severity-based secret exposure reports with remediation priorities.
Recommends credential rotation, git history cleanup, and prevention controls.
Provides CI, pre-commit, and .gitignore examples for ongoing protection.
limitations: Cannot prove whether a detected secret is active without access to the owning service.
May flag test data, examples, or placeholders that require human review.
Does not automatically revoke, rotate, or delete credentials.
History cleanup and force pushes require careful coordination outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Pre-release repository scan
use_cases.description: Check a repository before open source release or deployment and list secrets that need removal.

use_cases.title: Developer pull request review
use_cases.description: Review changed files for accidentally committed API keys, tokens, and private configuration values.

use_cases.title: Incident response triage
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized response plan after credentials are discovered in code or git history.

prompt_templates.title: Scan the current project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the secret scanner to inspect this repository for exposed credentials. Summarize any likely secrets and explain what I should do next.

prompt_templates.title: Review staged changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my staged changes for secrets, tokens, private keys, and unsafe environment files. Separate real risks from placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Audit git history
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the repository history for committed secrets. Report affected files, likely secret types, exposure scope, and cleanup recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan incident remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: A secret was committed and pushed. Build an incident response plan with rotation steps, access log checks, git history cleanup, and prevention controls.

output_examples.input: Scan this repository for committed credentials.
output: Critical: likely AWS access key in application configuration. Rotate it immediately and review cloud access logs.
High: GitHub token pattern in CI configuration. Replace it with a repository secret and reduce token scope.
Low: placeholder API key in documentation. No rotation required, but mark it as an example.

output_examples.input: Create remediation steps for a leaked private key.
output: Revoke the key from all servers that trust it.
Generate a new key pair outside the repository.
Remove the key from current files and git history.
Audit server logs for unauthorized access during the exposure window.

output_examples.input: Help prevent future leaks in this repo.
output_examples.output: Add secret scanning to pre-commit hooks and CI. Commit only environment templates, ignore real secret files, and document required variables.

best_practices: Run secret scanning before commits, releases, and public repository changes.
Rotate any credential that was committed, even after it is removed from the current branch.
Use managed secret stores and commit only safe templates such as .env.example.
anti_patterns: Treating deleted secrets as safe while they remain in git history.
Committing real .env files, private keys, or production database URLs.
Running destructive cleanup commands without coordinating with repository collaborators.

faq.question: Does this skill rotate leaked secrets for me?
faq.answer: No. It recommends rotation steps, but you must revoke and replace secrets in the owning service.

faq.question: Can it scan git history?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for history scanning with tools such as Gitleaks, TruffleHog, git-secrets, and detect-secrets.

faq.question: Will it detect every secret?
faq.answer: No. Secret scanning is pattern based and can miss unusual formats or encrypted values.

faq.question: How does it handle false positives?
faq.answer: It asks the assistant to review context and classify examples, placeholders, and test data separately from likely real secrets.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: The skill is a local analysis guide. Review tool commands before running them, especially commands that scan remotes or rewrite history.

faq.question: What should I do if a real secret is found?
faq.answer: Rotate the credential immediately, check access logs, remove it from files and history, and add prevention controls.
